answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the karst identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator pays for 229 runs and collects one. Because the reef index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the forge audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 229 answers need 229 separate inference runs with separate seeds. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
